question: Can prayers be combined without any reason, based on the hadith in Tirmidhi?
answer:
One other point before I go back: there is a common fatwa that everybody asks me about, and it is being propagated, and I am very hesitant to even say it, but only because people say this — that they find on Islamic websites and whatnot — that one can do jama' for no reason. One can do jama' for no reason. And they quote a hadith in Sunan at-Tirmidhi, which is authentic, that our Prophet ﷺ one day combined between dhuhr and asr, and then between maghrib and isha. And the rawi says: bi-ghayri khawfin wa la safar. There was no khawf, there was no safar, there was no rain, nothing going on, and he did it. And then he said: I wanted to make things easy for my Ummah; I did not want to put a haraj on my Ummah. Okay, so this hadith is in Tirmidhi, and the Prophet ﷺ did jama' without any reason.

Now, we all know that the non-Sunni firqah takes this as the default, and they do jama' every single day of their lives, right? We know this — or those of you who don't know, I just taught you this now.

This hadith is found in Tirmidhi. Tirmidhi himself says: in my entire book, every hadith I mention, you will find 'ulama that have accepted it, except for three hadith. Three hadith, I don't know any 'alim who ever accepted it. And he mentions this one as well. Accepted, meaning the fiqh ruling, that practiced this hadith: I don't know any 'alim that practiced this. This is before Tirmidhi; this is not a fatwa that was known before Imam at-Tirmidhi.

Nonetheless, some 'ulama throughout history after Tirmidhi did say, look, the hadith is clear. And so they said that once in a while, if you need to, then you may do jama'. **And I am very, very hesitant to open this door, and we should stick with the vast majority of scholars.**

Now, we are not talking about somebody who has an excuse. And I've had this come to me: a doctor is performing an eight-hour surgery. There are certain types of heart surgeries where you have to be there; you literally have to be there. And I actually — like, you guys tell me you don't even take a lunch break in that time? But the doctor said, no, we don't. I said, okay. I mean, if that is the case and the guy is going to die, that's a darurah of death. You don't even need to get a fatwa, obviously, in that situation.

But you're going shopping and you want to do jama'? That's it — you're going to open this door, and it's going to be a laugh and a joke. Like, just because of a football match, I don't want to... do jama' before. I understand, if there's a surgery or something, then you might even be able to make qiyas of a sandstorm or rain falling, like that. Okay, this is a circumstance. But to open this door and say, if life is awkward — shopping and whatnot — we should not do this. We have to pray on its proper time.
